reviewBoundary: New CET4/CET6-form whole-passage 10-gap shared banks with 15 full candidates, plus a new C1-form eight-gap word-formation passage. Same-author grammatical and lexical fit review, including all unused bank items and legitimate written variants. Invented examples are not reported empirical studies; no independent calibration claimed.

units.title: Planning a campus soup stall
units.instruction: Read the whole passage. Choose one word from the shared bank for each gap. Use each word at most once; five words are not needed.

materials.title: Planning a campus soup stall
materials.text:
When students opened a lunch stall for a campus festival, their first difficulty was deciding how much soup to make. They began with an ____1____ of the number of visitors, based on advance ticket sales. It was useful as a starting point, but it could not tell them exactly how many people would want lunch.

The team wanted to avoid food ____2____ without disappointing hungry customers. On the first day, ____3____ was strongest just after a morning lecture ended. The students sold nearly all their soup within twenty minutes, then waited through a quiet afternoon.

For the second day, they counted the number of ____4____ served during each half-hour period. They kept unused ____5____, such as dry lentils and unopened spices, apart from food that had already been cooked. This made it easier to see what could safely remain in stock for another day.

The new information helped them ____6____ their preparation times. It also showed that extra ____7____ were needed: several customers wanted to take soup to their friends rather than eat beside the stall.

The team posted a sign showing which soups were still ____8____ for purchase. They did not promise that every flavour would last until closing time. Instead, they kept the menu ____9____, changing it at short notice according to the supplies on hand.

After the festival, unused clean bowls were ____10____ to the supplier. The students had learned that a good plan was not simply a large quantity prepared in advance. It was a set of decisions that could respond to what happened during the day.

questions.explanation: An estimate of visitor numbers is a calculated approximation. Demand and waste do not describe that calculation, record takes a rather than an, and portions/ingredients/containers are plural. Adjust, briefly, available, flexible, misleading, predictable, returned and separate do not supply the singular count noun required after an.

Food waste is what excess preparation should avoid. Demand means requests rather than unwanted leftovers; an estimate or record would not be avoided as food disposal. Portions, ingredients and containers are physical units; the remaining bank items do not complete this noun phrase with the intended meaning.

Demand is customers' desire to buy, strongest after the lecture. Waste would mean discarded food, not sales pressure; portions, ingredients and containers are plural and do not agree with was. The count nouns estimate/record lack a determiner, while the adjectives, adverb and verbs do not name customer demand.

Portions are servings counted during periods. Ingredients are recipe components and containers are packaging, not the quantity explicitly served. Demand/waste are not countable servings; estimate/record would require a number of plural form. Other entries do not fit this plural noun slot.

Ingredients are exemplified by lentils and spices. Portions refers to served food and containers to packaging, neither matches the examples. The other items are not plural names for recipe components.

Adjust means change preparation times using new information. Record is grammatically possible but only logs times rather than changing the plan, while separate would divide times without that adaptation. Available, flexible, misleading and predictable are adjectives; briefly an adverb; the nouns and past returned do not complete helped them plus a base verb here.

Containers let customers carry soup away. Portions would mean extra servings and ingredients extra components, neither expresses the packaging need indicated by take soup to friends. Other entries do not provide the required plural physical receptacles.

Available for purchase means still obtainable. Flexible/predictable/misleading do not indicate remaining sale stock; separate describes division rather than availability. Returned is not appropriate with were still ... for purchase here, and the remaining parts of speech do not fit.

Flexible means changeable at short notice, explicitly explained after the comma. Predictable means expected, misleading deceptive, available obtainable and separate divided; none captures changing the menu to suit stock. The verbs, nouns and adverb do not provide the required quality.

Were returned to the supplier is the passive action taken with the bowls. None of the other words is the needed past participle for sending them back; base adjust/record/separate cannot follow were without inflection, and the adjectives/nouns/adverb do not express return.

units.title: Sharing a limited printing service
units.instruction: Read the whole passage. Choose one word from the shared bank for each gap. Use each word at most once; five words are not needed.

materials.title: Sharing a limited printing service
materials.text:
A university design workshop had three printers capable of producing large three-dimensional models. As more departments began to use them, the ____1____ of printing time became contentious. A single overnight job could delay several small projects, while a rule favouring short jobs could make ambitious models almost impossible to complete.

The coordinator began by listing the service's practical ____2____: machine capacity, staff hours and the time required to prepare each material. These limits could not be removed by asking users to cooperate more enthusiastically. Once they were visible, however, the discussion could focus on choices within them.

Printing slots were then ____3____ across departments according to a published trial schedule. Users were given modest ____4____ to release unused reservations early: doing so allowed them priority when requesting a later slot. Participation in the trial was ____5____, rather than a condition imposed on every department, so the coordinator was careful not to describe its users as representative of the whole university.

The schedule could not ____6____ every competing preference. Instead, the coordinator recorded which kinds of request were repeatedly postponed. The rules remained ____7____ during the first term, explicitly open to revision once the team understood their effects. Publishing both the rules and the reasons for exceptions made the process more ____8____ to users who had previously seen only an unexplained refusal.

One department proposed removing every spare interval from the schedule. Another argued that some ____9____ was needed so a machine failure would not disrupt all later work. The final plan retained a limited buffer, whose use would be reviewed rather than assumed to be permanently necessary.

The workshop also ____10____ records of the original requests, not merely the eventual bookings. Otherwise, a successful-looking schedule might conceal the projects that had never secured a place. The trial did not settle the argument about fairness. It gave that argument a more specific set of decisions to examine.

questions.explanation: Allocation of time is its assignment among competing jobs. Ambiguity means uncertainty of meaning, redundancy spare capacity, and constraints/incentives are plural. The other entries are verbs or adjectives, not the singular allocation noun required here.

Capacity, hours and preparation time are constraints, limits on service. Incentives are inducements rather than limits; allocation, ambiguity and redundancy are singular concepts. The other bank items do not name this plural set of practical restrictions.

Slots were distributed across departments, describing assignment under a schedule. Preserved means retained and does not explain spreading slots among departments. Reconcile and facilitate are base verbs; the nouns and adjectives do not give the required past-participle action.

Modest incentives reward early release through later priority. Constraints restrict action rather than encourage it, and the remaining noun concepts do not name those rewards. The adjective and verb entries cannot fill this plural-object slot.

Voluntary is directly contrasted with being imposed as a condition on all departments. Provisional means temporary, transparent clear, empirical evidence-based, exhaustive complete and marginal minor; none means chosen freely. The other entries have unsuitable grammatical roles.

Reconcile competing preferences means make them compatible. Facilitate means make an activity easier and does not naturally resolve conflicting preferences; the past forms distributed/preserved cannot follow could not. The remaining nouns and adjectives do not provide a base verb.

Provisional is defined by explicitly open to revision during the trial. Transparent refers to visibility, voluntary to free choice, empirical to evidence, exhaustive to completeness and marginal to limited importance; none supplies the stated tentative status.

Transparent describes rules and exceptions being understandable to users. Provisional and voluntary concern status and choice, empirical evidence, exhaustive completeness and marginal degree. None replaces the meaning of making reasons visible; the remaining items are not suitable adjectives.

Redundancy names spare capacity kept as a buffer for breakdowns. Allocation assigns time and ambiguity concerns meaning, while constraints/incentives name limits or rewards, not backup space. The other entries cannot serve as this uncountable concept after some was.

Preserved means kept original requests for later assessment. Distributed would spread them among recipients, not ensure the historical record remained; facilitate/reconcile lack past inflection, and the nouns/adjectives do not express retaining records.

units.title: Making a route guide useful
units.instruction: Use the word in brackets to form one word that fits each gap in the complete passage.

materials.title: Making a route guide useful
materials.text:
When our walking club redesigned its route guide, the editor began with a question about ____1____ (RELY). Could readers trust a short description to help them choose a suitable walk? A cheerful phrase such as "an easy morning" gave little information about steps or uneven ground.

The group invited a visitor to comment on the route's ____2____ (ACCESS). Her questions revealed several ____3____ (ASSUME) that regular walkers had never written down. They knew where the steep section began and where a gate opened, but newcomers did not.

To make a useful ____4____ (COMPARE) between routes, we replaced broad labels with specific distances and surface descriptions. The ____5____ (ACCURATE) of those details mattered more than giving every walk an equally attractive title.

Some obstacles had previously been almost ____6____ (VISIBLE) in our descriptions: they were never mentioned, even though they affected people's choices. A brief ____7____ (EXPLAIN) beside each route now identified its known limitations and the date of the latest check.

The editor retained final ____8____ (RESPONSIBLE) for publishing the guide, but asked members to report changes. No description could make the route suitable for everyone. It could, however, make the choice better informed.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 1 with a word formed from RELY.
questions.explanation: About requires the quality noun reliability. Reliable is an adjective and reliably an adverb.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 2 with a word formed from ACCESS.
questions.explanation: Both the quality accessibility and noun access can describe how the route can be used; both are accepted. Accessible and accessibly cannot follow the possessive as nouns here.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 3 with a word formed from ASSUME.
questions.explanation: Several requires plural count noun assumptions. Singular assumption and participle assuming do not fit.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 4 with a word formed from COMPARE.
questions.explanation: A useful requires a singular count noun comparison. Compare is a verb and comparative does not name the comparison in this construction.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 5 with a word formed from ACCURATE.
questions.explanation: The accuracy of details requires the quality noun. Accurate and accurately are adjective/adverb forms.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 6 with a word formed from VISIBLE.
questions.explanation: The colon explains that the obstacles were not mentioned, so almost invisible. Visibility is a noun and cannot complement been almost this way. Other semantically plausible unlisted variants remain reviewable.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 7 with a word formed from EXPLAIN.
questions.explanation: A brief explanation requires a singular noun. Explain is a verb and explained a participle.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 8 with a word formed from RESPONSIBLE.
questions.explanation: Retained final responsibility takes the noun responsibility. Responsible and responsibly are adjective/adverb forms.
